claim: Fold recognition has a satisfactory solution only for global alignments, while semi-global and local alignments are urgently needed.
falsifier: One can survey existing fold recognition methods and verify that global alignment methods are more mature than semi-global and local ones.

exclusions: Evidence is limited to the reported state of fold recognition methods; transfer to other recognition problems is unestablished.

title: Alignment type–satisfactory solution availability boundary

claim: The classical CN (Common Neighbors) method for link prediction scales as O(N ⟨k^2⟩), where N is number of nodes and ⟨k^2⟩ is the second moment of the degree distribution.
falsifier: One can implement CN on various networks and measure runtime scaling with N and degree moments.

conditions: assuming O(1) cost for graph data structure access and contribution addition
exclusions: Derived under idealized assumptions; actual performance may vary with implementation and graph structure.

title: CN link prediction method–computational complexity scaling theorem

claim: The NP-hardness proof for Euclidean k-Matching does not automatically establish NP-completeness because solution verification involves the Sum of Square Roots Problem, whose complexity is open.
falsifier: The verification complexity depends on the open SSRP; the NP-hardness part is testable.

conditions: verification requires comparing sums of square roots
exclusions: limited to the Euclidean metric and the specific reduction construction reported

title: Reduction from SAT–NP-completeness not established due boundary

claim: The 7Be(n,p) cross section is approximately 40% higher than previously recognized at low energies (below ~50 keV), but remains consistent with current evaluations and time-reversal data in the energy region relevant to Big Bang nucleosynthesis, resulting in only a minor improvement to the Cosmological Lithium Problem.
falsifier: The claim can be tested by independent measurements of the 7Be(n,p) cross section at low energies and by BBN network calculations using the reported cross section to quantify the change in predicted lithium abundance.

conditions: BBN-relevant energy region (consistent with time-reversal 7Li(p,n)7Be data)
exclusions: Evidence is limited to the specific 7Be(n,p) cross-section measurements performed at n_TOF and the comparison with previous evaluations and time-reversal data; transfer to other reactions or broader energy ranges is unestablished.

title: New measurement of–cross-section value relative principle
